# Ozen guide for AI agents

This file is the whole guide: the syntax, the standard actions, the diagnostics and the loop to
follow. The full reference is in `language.md`, `std.md` and `diagnostics.md` next to it.

## Quick syntax

<!-- file: salad.ozen -->
```ozen
// One recipe: ingredients first, then one step per line.
recipe salad(servings: 2) {
  ingredients {
    cabbage: 0.25 pcs per serving
    carrot: 0.5 pcs per serving
    dressing: Dressing 1 tbsp per serving
  }
  let cabbageCut = cabbage |> wash |> cut(julienne, 2 mm)
  let carrotCut = carrot |> peel |> cut(julienne, 2 mm)
  let mixed = toss([cabbageCut, carrotCut])
  let dressed = season(mixed, with: dressing)
}
```

<!-- run: ozen render --kind recipe --lang en salad.ozen -->
```text
# salad

## Ingredients
- cabbage, 0.5
- carrot, 1
- dressing, 30 ml

## Steps
1. Wash cabbage, then cut into julienne (2 mm).
2. Peel carrot, then cut into julienne (2 mm).
3. Toss cabbage, carrot.
4. Season cabbage, carrot with dressing.
```

- A file holds declarations: `recipe`, `menu`, `kitchen`, `import`, and the declarations of
  a library (`action`, `ingredient`, `unit` and others).
- `recipe NAME(servings: N) { ... }` declares a recipe. Parameters are written `name: value`
  or `name: Type`.
- `ingredients { name: [Type] AMOUNT [per serving] }` lists what the recipe uses. Without a
  type, the name is looked up as an ingredient of `std` (`carrot` is `Carrot`).
- `let name = expression` names the result of a step. Every value must be used exactly once;
  an unused value is a warning.
- A call is `action(x, positional, named: value)`. `x |> action(args)` is the same as
  `action(x, args)`, so steps chain from left to right. A call without arguments can drop
  `()`: `x |> peel`.
- `[a, b]` passes several ingredients to one step; the step makes a mixture of them.
- Amounts have units: `200 ml`, `0.5 pcs`, `1 tbsp`, `3 mm`, `15 min`, `170 degC`. A range is
  written `1..3 min`.
- A type can name the state it needs: `T<shape: peeled>`. Calling a step on an ingredient in
  another state is an error, for example `beat` before `crack`.
- `menu NAME(people: N) { ... }` combines recipes with `make RECIPE(args)` and plates them
  with `serve` and `plate`.
- `kitchen NAME { places {...} tools {...} tableware {...} }` describes the equipment, and
  `ozen debug schedule --entry MENU -k KITCHEN-FILE FILE` plans the work.
- Comments are `// to the end of the line` and `/* ... */`.

## Standard actions

| Action | Parameters | Required state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `beat` | `x: T<shape: cracked>` | x: shape: cracked |
| `blend` | `x: T<shape != inShell>` | x: shape != inShell |
| `boil` | `x: T, time: Time in 0 s<..` | any |
| `boilWater` | `x: Water` | any |
| `chill` | `x: T, time: Time in 0 s<..` | any |
| `clean` | `t: Tool` | any |
| `combine` | `xs: [T]` | any |
| `cookRice` | `x: Rice<prep has soaked>` | x: prep has soaked |
| `crack` | `x: T<shape: inShell, doneness: raw>` | x: shape: inShell, doneness: raw |
| `cut` | `x: T<shape: peeled \| shape: cut \| SkinEdible, shape: whole>, style: CutStyle, size: Length in 0 mm<.. = 3 mm` | x: shape: peeled or shape: cut or SkinEdible, shape: whole |
| `deepFry` | `x: T<shape != inShell>, oil: Oil, time: Time in 0 s<.., temp: Temperature = 170 degC` | x: shape != inShell |
| `discard` | `x: T` | any |
| `dissolve` | `x: T<shape != inShell>` | x: shape != inShell |
| `drain` | `x: T<prep has washed \| prep has soaked>` | x: prep has washed or prep has soaked |
| `fillet` | `x: T<RoundFish>` | x: RoundFish |
| `fry` | `x: T<shape != inShell>, time: Time in 0 s<.., heat: Heat = medium` | x: shape != inShell |
| `layer` | `x: T<shape != inShell>` | x: shape != inShell |
| `loosen` | `x: T<Noodle>` | x: Noodle |
| `mix` | `x: T<shape != inShell>` | x: shape != inShell |
| `parboil` | `x: T, time: Time in 0 s<..` | any |
| `peel` | `x: T<Peelable, shape: whole \| shape: inShell, doneness >= done>` | x: Peelable, shape: whole or shape: inShell, doneness >= done |
| `plate` | `x: T` | any |
| `rest` | `x: T, time: Time in 0 s<..` | any |
| `season` | `x: T<shape != inShell>, with: T<Seasoning>` | x: shape != inShell; with: Seasoning |
| `simmer` | `x: T, time: Time in 0 s<.., heat: Heat = low` | any |
| `soak` | `x: T, time: Time in 0 s<.. = 30 min` | any |
| `store` | `x: T` | any |
| `tear` | `x: T<LeafyVegetable>` | x: LeafyVegetable |
| `toss` | `x: T<shape != inShell>` | x: shape != inShell |
| `warm` | `x: T` | any |
| `wash` | `x: T` | any |
| `whip` | `x: T<Liquid, shape != inShell>` | x: Liquid, shape != inShell |
| `wipe` | `p: Place` | any |

| SYN014 | `macroBody` | The macro body is not well formed |

## Work loop

1. Write or change the recipe in a `.ozen` file.
2. Run `ozen check --format json FILE` and read every diagnostic.
3. Fix every error (severity `error`) and rerun the check until it reports 0 errors.
4. Run `ozen render --kind recipe FILE` and read the recipe text to see that it says what you meant.
